summary: Implemented open_device_terminal (Windows Terminal via wt.exe, arguments always passed as separate tokens) and extended the system tray with per-device Open Terminal / Open Service shortcuts, wiring up the Terminal buttons left disabled since WU013/WU014. open_device_service already shipped in WU015 (pulled forward because that WU's own acceptance criteria required it), so this WU completes the pair. cargo test 155/155 (152 prior + 3 new).
completed: platform/terminal.rs: build_terminal_args() (pure, unit-tested) builds the wt.exe argument list as separate tokens (new-tab -- ssh.exe [-p <port>] <user>@<host>); launch_ssh_terminal() spawns wt.exe detached, never requests/stores a password.
commands/launch.rs: open_device_terminal(deviceId) command, translating launch failures into the standard ApplicationError shape with remediation.

platform/tray.rs: extracted build_menu()/build_devices_submenu()/build_device_submenu(); tray now has a 'Devices' submenu with per-device 'Open Terminal' and one 'Open <service>' per enabled service. Added rebuild_device_menu(app), wired into create_device/update_device/delete_device so the tray stays in sync without a restart. Also wired the pre-existing 'Refresh All' tray item to the real scheduler::refresh_all instead of its WU001 placeholder log line.

features/devices/DeviceDetailScreen.tsx and features/dashboard/DeviceCard.tsx: Terminal buttons now call open_device_terminal with a loading spinner and inline error, replacing the disabled placeholder state.

3 new Rust unit tests for build_terminal_args (default port omits -p, non-default port passes -p as a separate token, a host containing shell metacharacters still becomes exactly one argument since no shell is ever spawned).
Verified cargo build (clean) and cargo test (155/155); npm run build and npm run lint (0 errors, 3 pre-existing warnings) since frontend call sites changed too.

validationCommands.summary: 155/155 unit tests passed (152 prior + 3 new terminal-arg tests).
0 errors, 3 pre-existing HMR-granularity warnings (unrelated to this WU).

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: SSH terminal sessions open in Windows Terminal for both Raspberry Pis
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: open_device_terminal looks up the device and calls launch_ssh_terminal(host, sshPort, sshUsername), which spawns `wt.exe new-tab -- ssh.exe [-p <port>] <user>@<host>` detached; wired into both DeviceCard and DeviceDetailScreen's Terminal buttons.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Home Assistant and Personal Finance services open in the default browser
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: open_device_service (WU015) remains the launch path from the Services screen, DeviceDetailScreen's service tiles, and now also the tray's per-device 'Open <service>' items, which call tauri_plugin_opener::open_url directly.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: No command string is ever built via interpolation; all arguments are passed separately to the process API
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: build_terminal_args returns a Vec<String> passed to Command::args(); the_destination_is_a_single_argument_never_a_joined_command_string test confirms a host with shell metacharacters (';', 'rm -rf /') still produces exactly 4 argument tokens with the destination as one opaque token, since std::process::Command never invokes a shell.

notes: Risk score: 25/100 (low-medium). Rationale: introduces one new process-spawning surface (wt.exe) beyond the already-audited ssh.exe path, but follows the identical separate-arguments convention and has direct unit coverage of the argument-construction logic; the tray's menu-event dispatch duplicates a small amount of open-URL/launch-terminal logic outside the Tauri command layer (tray clicks don't go through invoke()), which is necessary because tray event handlers run in a different call path, not a design smell.

Scope note: fixed the tray's 'Refresh All' item, which had been left as a WU001-era placeholder log line ('Monitoring is implemented in a later work unit') -- monitoring didn't exist yet when that comment was written, and it's the same file (platform/tray.rs) being substantially rewritten for this WU's actual per-device-shortcuts scope, so leaving a known-stale placeholder in place while touching everything around it would have been worse than fixing the one-line gap.

Terminal-launch failure messaging assumes Windows Terminal is either present (ships with Windows 11 by default) or absent (remediation suggests the Microsoft Store); could not exercise the actual failure path in this sandboxed dev environment without wt.exe/a real SSH target, so that branch is covered by the ApplicationError mapping and manual code review rather than an end-to-end failure test.
Embedded terminal UI remains explicitly out of MVP scope per this WU's packet; Open Terminal always hands off to the user's own Windows Terminal installation.
